harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Built an Ansible project on node1 that creates a "Fleet Internal CA", issues a node2 TLS certificate (CN=node2, SAN=DNS:node2/IP:10.100.75.11), configures node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 via a systemd-managed TLS service, and installs the CA as a trusted system CA on both node1 and node2. Verified cross-node HTTPS trust in both directions, then completed the mandatory boot-identity restart/recovery protocol on all three managed nodes.
actions_performed: Bootstrapped pip and Ansible 2.9.27 (with the cryptography module) on node1 since no package repos were configured
Wired passwordless SSH between node1 and node2 using the cluster-provided keypair, and added ansible.cfg so the elevated Ansible run could use it

Wrote an Ansible project (~/ca-tls-ansible on node1) with roles ca_authority (CA key + self-signed cert, node2 key/CSR/signed cert via openssl_privatekey/openssl_csr/openssl_certificate), ca_trust (installs the CA cert into /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and runs update-ca-trust), and https_service (deploys key+cert chain, a Python TLS HTTP server, a fleet-https.service systemd unit, and opens firewalld 8443/tcp) on node2
Ran the playbook (site.yml) end-to-end idempotently against inventory groups ca=node1 and web=node2

Verified CA subject 'Fleet Internal CA' with CA:TRUE basic constraint, node2 cert chaining to it with correct SAN, and curl with no extra flags trusting https://node2:8443 from both node1 and node2 via the system trust store; confirmed firewalld persists the 8443 rule

Captured healthy baselines, then restarted node1, node2, and node3 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polled each until exec access returned, and proved changed /proc/sys/kernel/random/boot_id values plus post-restart recovery (CA/cert files intact, fleet-https auto-started and enabled, firewall rule persisted, cross-node HTTPS still trusted, node3 baseline state unchanged)

evidence.requirement: Create CA 'Fleet Internal CA' on node1
evidence.summary: ca_authority role generates CA key + self-signed cert with CN=Fleet Internal CA and CA:TRUE; playbook run created it; openssl x509 confirms subject and basic constraints on node1

evidence.requirement: Issue node2 a TLS certificate from that CA
evidence.summary: node2 key/CSR/cert generated and signed by the CA (ownca provider); served cert verified subject=CN=node2, issuer=CN=Fleet Internal CA, SAN=DNS:node2/IP:10.100.75.11

evidence.requirement: Configure node2 to serve HTTPS on port 8443 with that certificate
evidence.summary: https_service role deployed cert/key, systemd unit fleet-https, and firewalld 8443/tcp rule; fleet-https active/listening on 8443; cross-node curl from node1 to https://10.100.75.11:8443 succeeded after firewall fix

evidence.requirement: Install CA as trusted system CA on node1 and node2
evidence.summary: CA cert placed in /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors and update-ca-trust run on both nodes; curl with no --cacert flag trusts https://node2:8443 from both node1 (system-wide) and node2 (localhost hostname); trust list shows 'Fleet Internal CA' anchor on node2
Ansible 2.9.27 installed and used to run site.yml (roles ca_authority, ca_trust, https_service) against inventory covering node1 and node2, with a clean idempotent second run

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 192f6cab...; systemctl reboot issued and disconnected; post-reboot boot_id changed to 1fd63285...; CA files, trust anchor, and cross-node HTTPS trust all confirmed intact after restart

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id d72bd4ec...; systemctl reboot issued; post-reboot boot_id changed to 3071ef47...; fleet-https active/enabled, firewalld 8443 rule persisted, CA trust anchor present, and cross-node HTTPS from node1 verified working post-restart

evidence.requirement: node3 restart evidence: baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovery
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 7051d0bc...; systemctl reboot issued (stream closed on disconnect); post-reboot boot_id changed to 0dc8d9e4...; node3 state (ssh inactive) matches pre-restart baseline, confirming clean recovery of its unchanged configuration
